limitations: No empty-neighborhood policy is defined in section2/algorithm4; Kth-neighbor existence and nonzero scale are mathematical preconditions, not an observed exception handler.

author: Jont B. Allen; Lawrence R. Rabiner (Bell Laboratories)
edition: Proceedings of the IEEE65(11),1558–1564, author-hosted reprint
section_read: PDF all7pages; sectionsII–IX; rendered p3(1560) Fig3/equations4.2–4.6 and p6(1563) sectionVII/equations7.1–7.4

confirmed.objects: discrete time signal x(n), shifted finite windows, uniformly spaced analysis frequencies, STFT samples
confirmed.relations: overlap-add depends on sum of shifted windows; modified spectra may require longer FFT padding
confirmed.invariant: reconstruction of unchanged input up to known scale, under window sampling conditions
confirmed.actual_source_inputs: Hamming N=100,Fs=10000 leads B=200Hz and hop25 at stated42dB criterion; Fig3 depicts N/4 shifts; sectionV.B requires L>=N+N0-1 for modified response support

limitations: The paper distinguishes unmodified recoverability from adequacy after spectral modification; exact reconstruction alone does not certify arbitrary changes.
N/4 is tied to Hamming and a42dB criterion, not a universal hop rule.
Integer sample-time and fixed-rate analysis do not directly prescribe irregular timestamp processing.
The paper does not solve MKV decoding, tokenizer requirements, or current librosa stream defaults.
All arithmetic counterexamples below are researcher constructed and not original paper experiments.
Source OCR has corruption; key OLA and sampling equations were checked in rendered pages.
